evals.prompt: Run an IaC scan over our infra/terraform tree before I `terraform apply` — flag anything that would expose S3 publicly or open a security group to 0.0.0.0/0.
evals.expected_output: Severity-grouped finding table by file:line with resource, issue, recommendation, plus a 2-3 line fix snippet for each high-severity finding; summary written under .vulnetix/iac/.
expectations: Reads .vulnetix/capabilities.yaml and verifies derived.has_iac: true (or that --paths was supplied) before scanning
Renders results as a markdown table with columns: Severity | File:Line | Resource | Issue | Recommendation, grouped by file
Includes a 2-3 line fix code snippet for every high-severity finding (open SGs, public S3, IAM wildcards)
If binaries.terraform or binaries.tofu is true, suggests running `terraform plan -no-color | head -200` for context but does NOT execute `terraform apply`

evals.prompt: Audit just these two files for misconfig: `--paths k8s/prod-deployment.yaml ops/main.tf`. I want a compliance-friendly report.
evals.expected_output: Static-only misconfig findings for the two explicit paths, no false claim of runtime evaluation, output grouped by file with recommendations.
expectations: Passes the explicit --paths through to `vulnetix iac --paths "k8s/prod-deployment.yaml ops/main.tf" -o json` instead of scanning the whole tree
Detects k8s misconfigurations only on top-level YAML kinds matching common workload types (per edge-cases note)
Calls out that detection is static — cannot evaluate runtime `var.environment == "prod"` interpolation, reports both branches
Groups findings per file in the rendered markdown table and includes plaintext-secret / missing-tag / unpinned-provider checks where applicable
Writes `.vulnetix/iac.<timestamp>.json` raw output and `.vulnetix/iac/<timestamp>.summary.yaml` with finding counts
Does NOT delegate to SAST or container-scan even though source/Dockerfiles may be nearby

evals.prompt: Gate our PR — fail loud if any critical IaC findings exist in the diff (public bucket, IAM wildcard, plaintext secret).
evals.expected_output: Critical-severity findings surfaced first with file:line, blocking guidance, and a clear pass/fail verdict suitable for CI gating.
expectations: Aborts early with a clear message if derived.has_iac is false and no --paths is given (no silent empty result)
Prioritises critical findings (public S3/GCS, IAM wildcard `*`, plaintext secrets, unencrypted state backends, open security groups) at the top of the report
Each critical row includes a 2-3 line fix snippet (e.g. `acl = "private"`, restricted CIDR, KMS-encrypted backend)
Notes the limitation that pre-existing infra not present in IaC (`terraform import` candidates) is not detected
Writes raw JSON to `.vulnetix/iac.<timestamp>.json` and summary to `.vulnetix/iac/<timestamp>.summary.yaml`
Does not auto-run `terraform plan` or `terraform apply` — only suggests `terraform plan -no-color | head -200` for human review
